Bedford County by the numbers

Who records deeds in Bedford County, Pennsylvania?

The Recorder of Deeds division of the combined Register and Recorder office handles every deed, mortgage, lease, survey, financing statement and right of way in Bedford County. It is in Room 106 on the first floor of the Bedford County Courthouse, 200 S Juliana St, Bedford, PA 15522. The phone is (814) 623-4836 and the email is randr@bedfordcountypa.org.

The county describes its holdings as permanent records dating back to 1771, the year Bedford County was created from part of Cumberland County. The office also keeps records for several neighbors listed on the county site: Huntingdon, Somerset, Centre, Cambria, Blair and Fulton. Seven public workstations let title searchers, lenders and genealogists look documents up on their own, though staff do not run title searches for visitors.

Closing agents can file electronically through Simplifile and CSC, so a seller usually never visits the counter. The office also offers FraudSleuth, a free service that lets owners confirm which recordings are authorized.

What are the office hours and same-day recording cutoff?

The counter is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. and closed on designated county holidays. Same-day recording stops at 4:00 p.m., and the register and recorder page describes recording as taking place from 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

Plan around that earlier cutoff. For a quick close, ask the title company to submit the deed well before 4:00 p.m. rather than carrying paper in at the end of the day.

  • Same-day cutoff: 4:00 p.m.
  • Mail goes to Recorder of Deeds Division, Bedford County Courthouse, 200 S Juliana St, Room 106, Bedford, PA 15522.
  • Every mailed filing needs a self-addressed stamped envelope for return of the documents.

How much does it cost to record a deed in Bedford County?

A deed is $59.75 on the fee bill effective November 20, 2025. That figure already includes the state and county taxes the schedule folds in, and it assumes a document with no more than four names and four pages. Each additional name adds $0.50 and each additional page adds $2.00.

Bedford County recording fees, from the Recorder's fee bill effective November 20, 2025
DocumentFee
Deed$59.75
Mortgage$59.75
Satisfaction piece$59.75
Release of mortgage$61.75
Assignment of mortgage$61.75
Easement$59.75
Power of attorney$18.50
Photocopy, per page$0.25
Certified copy$1.00 plus $0.25 a page
Soldier discharge (DD-214)Free

Fees have to be exact. The office cannot refund and keeps overages of $5.00 or less, and if an overage is larger the document comes back. No more than five documents can ride on a single check.

What does the realty transfer tax cost in Bedford County?

The county brochure states a state tax of 1% and a local tax of 1% of the consideration, due when the deed is recorded. That makes 2% in total, and it is paid on top of the recording fee. The office accepts checks, money orders, cash, and credit or debit cards, and checks are made payable to the Register Recorder named on the fee bill.

One check is enough: the county says it does not require separate checks for transfer tax and recording fees. If the property spans more than one municipality or school district, the deed has to state in whole numbers how the local tax is divided between them.

  • Deeds must show the true consideration or carry a completed Statement of Value.
  • Deeds, mortgages and assignments all need a signed Certificate of Residence.
  • The county web page links a Common Level Ratio sheet and the realty transfer tax forms.

What does Bedford County look like to a home seller?

Bedford County is the largest of the four counties on these pages by land, at 1,017 square miles, but the smallest by population. Census QuickFacts estimates 47,480 residents for 2025, roughly flat against the 2020 base of 47,567, and a density of about 47 people per square mile. The county seat is Bedford, and the landscape is ridge and valley country, with Blue Knob the highest mountain and limestone quarries in the Morrison Cove area.

Housing is mostly owner-occupied. QuickFacts counts 23,836 housing units, 19,750 households and an owner-occupied rate of 77.5%. The median value of an owner-occupied home was $179,000 for 2020 to 2024, median gross rent was $784, and only 75 building permits were issued in 2025. Households with a broadband subscription came to 83.1%, lower than the other three counties compared here, which a buyer working remotely may weigh.

Historic travel routes shaped the county. The old Forbes Road is now US 30, and the Pennsylvania Turnpike, I-70, I-76 and I-99 all run through. Bedford Springs once drew wealthy vacationers in the late 19th century.

Which other documents does the Bedford County office record, and at what price?

Beyond deeds and mortgages, the fee bill lists a long run of real estate and miscellaneous instruments. Most affidavits, agreements, covenants, declarations, notices, restrictions and orders are $18.50. Amendments, cancellations, modifications, subordinations and terminations run $20.50, and leases of 30 years or longer, installment sales agreements, memorandums and oil and gas leases are $59.75.

Maps and plans are priced separately. A plat under 24 inches is $9.00 and one over 24 inches is $13.00. State highway and mining plans are $16.50 for the first page, with additional pages at $3.00. UCC financing statements and their ancillary filings are $100.00 each.

  • Notary public bond and commission: $39.50, which includes the commission tax and writ tax.
  • Notary name change or address change: $18.50.
  • Clean and Green filing: $18.50.
  • Partial release: $61.75.

For a home seller the practical lines are the deed, the mortgage satisfaction and any easement. If a title search turns up an old right of way or an unreleased mortgage, those are the instruments your closing agent will ask the office to record or clear.

What should a Bedford County seller check before the deed goes in?

Start with the paperwork the office will reject if it is missing. Every deed, mortgage and assignment needs a Certificate of Residence completed and signed, and the deed must state the true consideration or come with a fully completed Statement of Value. The county also asks that fees be exact, so confirm the number with the office or your closing agent instead of rounding up.

Next, check how the sale will be paid. Settle ahead of time who brings the 2% tax and the recording fee, whether the closing runs through a title company or privately. The brochure says all fees and taxes are payable in advance, so a deed cannot be recorded first and paid later.

  • Confirm the grantee name and mailing address spelling.
  • Ask which municipality and school district the parcel falls in.
  • Call (814) 623-4836 with questions about the fee bill.
  • Keep a recorded copy for your records after closing.

How do you get a copy of a recorded Bedford County document?

Records can be viewed online through the Recorder of Deeds Records Online link on the county page, or at the public workstations in Room 106. Photocopies are $0.25 a page at the counter, pages larger than 11 by 17 inches are $2.00, and a certified copy is $1.00 plus $0.25 for each page.

The office does not take part in title searches and cannot offer legal advice, so the county suggests an attorney for questions about what a document means. Originals go back to whoever presented them, unless the filer directs otherwise, and mailed documents must come with a postage-paid return envelope. Military discharge papers are kept confidential, available only to the veteran or a veterans organization, and recording a DD-214 and any certified copies are free.

It is $59.75 for a deed with up to four names and four pages, under the fee bill effective November 20, 2025. Each added name is $0.50 and each added page is $2.00.

Is the transfer tax included in the Bedford County deed fee?

The fee bill says its listed fees include state and county taxes. The realty transfer tax itself is 1% state and 1% local of the consideration, collected at recording, so ask the office how your deed's total is calculated.

Can I record a Bedford County deed electronically?

Yes. The office accepts e-recording through Simplifile and CSC, along with mail and in-person filing. Most sellers leave this to the title company.

When does same-day recording stop in Bedford County?

Same-day recording stops at 4:00 p.m. even though the office stays open until 4:30 p.m. Call (814) 623-4836 if a closing is running late.

Does the Bedford County office return my original deed?

Yes. Originals go back to the person who presented them unless the office is told otherwise, and mailed documents need a postage-paid return envelope.
